## Pass 1

Changes are listed as unit · field · severity · what was wrong · what was done. Units are numbered from 0, as in units.json. Every edit was made by script (scratchpad review1_edit.py and review1_edit2.py for units.json, review1_lemmas.py for new-lemmas.txt). Each script asserts the old text before it replaces it. No glyph code, glyph order, q, rubric flag or restored flag was changed. One regrouping was made (U12, below), and the q of both new words is Budge's own.

- U13 · l, i, n · major · The note opened "The papyrus writes nty pr; read nty n pr", which is the misprint form, but in the same sentence it said the correction "is not sure". The misprint rule applies only where the sense allows one reading. Here, what stands can be read: nty (with the man classifier, so persons) with pr as the stative, 'who come forth from their guard'. So the rule is not met. · l → "… · who · come-forth · from · guarding-their"; i → "…, who come forth from their custody(?)". The note now explains nty and pr as written and translates what stands, says it sits awkwardly with the keepers' task, and offers the dropped negative n ('from whose guard there is no coming out') as the alternative. It also says neither reading is sure.
- U12 · words, l, i, n · major · rdi n·sn nb-r-ḏr was read as a relative form rdi, 'to whom the Lord to the Limit has given', with n·sn 'to them' and 'charge' supplied in i. The signs read more simply as rdi·n sn nb-r-ḏr: a sḏm·n·f with the dependent pronoun sn 'them' as its object, standing before the noun subject as dependent pronouns do. That gives 'the Lord to the Limit has set them (to serve him …)', with nothing supplied, and the r + infinitive of U13 follows on naturally. · Budge's w77 + w78 are joined as rdi·n (D21 D37 N35; morph rdi + sḏm·n·f; q "0:1-2", the drafter's join rule), and w79 stands alone as sn (O34 z, N35 n, Z2 det; lemma sn; q "0:1:2", Budge's). l → "… · has-set · them · the-Lord-to-the-Limit". i → "… from those keepers who inspect, whom the Lord to the Limit has set". The note explains the form and keeps the relative-form reading as the alternative. new-lemmas: BROADEN sn with the dependent pronoun.
- U13 · n · minor · "n·f, 'him' being the one in their charge" did not fit the main clause. With rdi·n sn nb-r-ḏr, 'him' is the Lord to the Limit, and 'his enemies' are his. · Changed to say so.
- U12 · n · minor · The note said "m-ꜥ nnw pw iryw sipw rdi n·sn nb-r-ḏr in red", but nb-r-ḏr (w80) carries no rubric flag. · → "… rdi·n sn in red; nb-r-ḏr is in black."
- U12 · l, i · minor · The note calls nḥm·k a sḏm·f that asks for what it names, but l "rescue-you" and i "rescue the Osiris Ani" read as an imperative. Pass 1 of ani-017-c ruled the same way for dr·tn. · l → "may-rescue-you · …"; i → "may you rescue the Osiris Ani, …".
- U5 · words[ṯꜣi] reading, say, morph; n · minor · The word was keyed to a new lemma ṯꜣi, "to seize", which duplicates the known ṯꜣ, "to seize, despoil, steal". Its two reeds were read as i, although the house reads two reeds as y (ky, pwy, ꜣny). · reading → ṯꜣy, say → tjay, lemma → ṯꜣ. The note now reads "ṯꜣy 'who seizes', a participle of ṯꜣ 'seize' … two reeds y". The ṯꜣi entry is removed from new-lemmas.txt.
- U13 · morph (sꜣwt, sꜣwt·sn) · minor · The sꜣw key collision. The drafter keyed the noun 'guard, custody' to sꜣw, which is "Sais" in the glossary, and broadened sꜣw with a verb. Glossary keys are bare lemma spellings: assemble() looks up G[lemma], and no published key carries a qualifier such as "sꜣw (guard)". Homographs share one key as "a second word of the same spelling". Both occurrences here are the noun sꜣwt, and sꜣwt is already a known key (Asyut). · Lemma → sꜣwt in both words. new-lemmas: "BROADEN sꜣwt — a second word of the same spelling: guard, watch, custody (noun f.; from sꜣw 'guard, keep watch over'; …)" replaces the sꜣw broaden. The reading matches its key, and no verb sense is filed that the text does not use. The note says sꜣwt is "the noun 'guard, custody'".
- U13 · n · minor · ddyw was called "the plural participle of rdi" and its doubled stem was left unexplained. · → "the plural imperfective participle of rdi … with its doubled stem dd" (the ani-017-c ruling).
- U11 · i · minor · "whose body is the company of the primeval gods(?)". 'company' is not in the Egyptian, and it echoes Budge's "cycle / company of the gods". · → "whose body is the primeval gods(?)".
- about · minor · "the god who devours souls" uses Budge's 'soul' for bꜣ, and the verb is not the text's. · → "the god who seizes the ba and swallows hearts".
- about, U0, U3 · n · style · Part 3's last statement was quoted as 'I am his ba in the midst of the Two Tjafi'. The published i is 'I am his ba, who is in the midst of the Two Tjafi'. · Quoted as published.
- U16 · i · style · "I do not lie weary". 'lie' is not in wrd. · → "I do not grow weary …".
- U5, U9, U10 · n · style · The background sentences claimed more than the text supports: "a danger every spell of protection reckons with", "Seth … is the god who devours the dead", and the gloss "names the devourer as a form of the earth god's power". · Rewritten: "A devourer of the dead is a danger the spells of this book often guard against."; "Seth … is named here as the devourer."; "The second gloss gives the devourer another name, as the ba of the earth god."
- U14 · n · style · "in all four clauses that follow". The four clauses include this one. · → "in all four clauses of this list".
- U12, U13 · n · style · Both notes went over 1600 characters after the changes above. · Tightened: the U12 alternative is now one sentence, and the U13 nty/pr discussion is merged with the readings of nty and pr.
- new-lemmas.txt · nsb, ḥwꜣw, pꜣwt, bwt, BROADEN bgꜣ, skr, iꜣt, smꜣ, sꜣw · minor · These entries described the signs of this occurrence ("written with the tongue ns", "the pustule", "the flying pintail and round loaves", "the bird of bad things", "the weary man", "the boat on a sledge", "the leg crossed by a knife and the house", "with the house sign", "the seated man holding a stick, A47"). · The sign descriptions are removed.
- new-lemmas.txt · smꜣ-wr, pꜣwt, iꜣt · minor · These entries carried line-pinned doubts ("reading of the first sign pair uncertain", "reading doubtful", "reading and sense uncertain"). · Removed. The (?) on the meaning stays, and the notes on U10, U11 and U13 keep the doubts.
- new-lemmas.txt · sip, pꜣwt, bgꜣ, ḏt · minor · sip claimed a noun "sipw 'inventory'" that cannot be supported, and pinned "participle sipw 'who inspect'" to this text. pꜣwt added "the first company of gods", which is an invented gloss with a Budge echo. bgꜣ added "the state of the dead", which is an interpretation. ḏt carried this line's "ḏt·f 'his body'". · sip → "to inspect, check, examine (verb; Budge: sàpu)". pꜣwt → "the primeval gods (?)". bgꜣ → "perhaps also weariness, inertness (?) (noun; imyw bgꜣ …)". The ḏt example is dropped.
- new-lemmas.txt · smꜣ-wr · style · "a god named as the ba of Geb" → "a god called the ba of Geb".

Severity count: 2 major, 11 minor (three of them grouped new-lemmas items), 6 style.

### Refused findings
- U4, the gap note: it says in general terms that other papyri, among them Nebseni (Budge's source for the passage), have a long passage here that Ani's scribe left out, "the rest of this gloss and more of the commentary". It gives no content. The line and page numbers come from the packet. Kept.
- U3, ꜥḥꜥ·n·w with ·w as the later 3rd plural suffix and ḫpr as stative: the known gloss of ·w covers this, and the note says the reading is not sure. Kept.
- U2, ꜥḥꜥ·n ḥpt·n with no subject written and 'one' supplied: the doubt and the alternative (n as 'to') are in the note. Kept.
- U3/U4, ṯꜣfy with Z9 phon and an empty tr (the validator warns): this is the published coding of the same word in ani-017-c U34. Kept.
- U5 nsb, U13 ḫftyw·f and nty, U12 nḥm·k: phon signs marked "not read" (w, ꜣ, ꜥ). This is the published practice, and each note says so. Kept.
- U12, U13, U17: double reeds coded i+i in some words and y+y in ddyw. Both codings are published (107 and 26 cases). Kept.
- U11, pꜣwt against Budge's paut = psḏt: the signs (pintail pꜣ, w, t, loaves) do not write psḏt, and the note says why and calls the reading doubtful. Kept.
- U6 skry as the bark of Sokar, U7 bgꜣ, U13/U15 iꜣt, U16 smꜣwt: each is hedged in l, i and the note. Budge's forms are given. Kept.
- U13 ꜣḫ n·f 'be useful to him' against Budge's 'protect': the crested ibis with ḫ writes ꜣḫ, and the note says why. Kept.
- U17 n·i 'to me' against Budge's 'by me': n marks the person affected, and the note says so. Kept.
- U9 swty keyed to stẖ: the known entry gives "written stẖ or swt", and say is "Seth", as in the published parts. Kept.
- U18 restored flag: only F34 and the stroke under it (Budge's [àb]) carry it, and the note says they are restored. Kept.
- Budge-isms and remembered wording: after the changes above, none remain in l / i / about. "triumphant", "soul", "Tchafi", "Seb", "defects" occur only in notes, as Budge's renderings. "true of voice", "the Lord to the Limit", "Djedu", "Two Tjafi(?)" and the question "What, then, is it?" match ani-017-c and the known glosses. Kept.

Re-check after editing (scratchpad check.py): OK. The sign sequence equals the established w0..w119, and rubric flags match the packet sign for sign. Restored flags are unchanged (compared with a copy taken before editing). Morph coverage and q indices are exact. Every det has an empty tr. Every lemma is known or new. Every BROADEN key exists, and every new entry is used. The replica build passes 19 units. Remaining warnings: Budge named in notes (expected); U12 and U13 notes at 1614 and 1790 characters (long clauses); Z9 phon with an empty tr in ṯꜣfy (published coding).
